name: Frodo's Journey
description: From Bag End to Mount Doom at real scale: 1,779 miles (about 2,863 km), with mileposts from the Éowyn Challenge, based on Karen Wynn Fonstad's The Atlas of Middle-earth. Heights are invented for the game.

bag-end.name: Bag End
bag-end.text: The party is over, the house is sold, and a small, heavy thing rides in Frodo's pocket.

farmer-maggot.name: Farmer Maggot's Farm
farmer-maggot.text: A gruff farmer, fierce dogs, and a basket of mushrooms for the road.

bucklebury-ferry.name: Bucklebury Ferry
bucklebury-ferry.text: Across the Brandywine by raft in the fog.

crickhollow.name: Crickhollow
crickhollow.text: A snug house and a conspiracy unmasked: your friends are coming with you.

old-forest.name: The Old Forest
old-forest.text: The trees here remember and do not like hobbits much.

bombadil.name: Tom Bombadil's House
bombadil.text: A cheerful singer, a golden-haired lady and a day of rain.

barrow-downs.name: The Barrow-downs
barrow-downs.text: Fog, standing stones and a cold voice in the dark.

bree.name: Bree
bree.text: A crowded inn, a careless song, a ranger watching from the corner.

midgewater.name: Midgewater Marshes
midgewater.text: Days of midges, reeds and wet feet.

weathertop.name: Weathertop
weathertop.text: Old ruins on a bare hill, and a night you won't forget.

last-bridge.name: The Last Bridge
last-bridge.text: A green elf-stone on the bridge: a sign that friends are near.

stone-trolls.name: The Stone Trolls
stone-trolls.text: Three trolls turned to stone long ago. Sam makes up a song about them.

ford-of-bruinen.name: Ford of Bruinen
ford-of-bruinen.text: The river rises in white horses.

rivendell.name: Rivendell
rivendell.text: A hidden valley of music and long councils. Nine walkers set out from here.

hollin.name: Hollin
hollin.text: Holly trees and silent ruins. No birds sing here.

caradhras.name: Caradhras
caradhras.text: The mountain throws snow at you until you turn back.

moria-gate.name: The Doors of Durin
moria-gate.text: A riddle on the doors, a lake that stirs, and then the long dark.

khazad-dum-bridge.name: Bridge of Khazad-dûm
khazad-dum-bridge.text: A narrow stone bridge over a bottomless drop. Not everyone crosses it.

dimrill-dale.name: Dimrill Dale
dimrill-dale.text: Daylight at last, and a still lake that holds the stars.

lothlorien.name: Lothlórien
lothlorien.text: Golden trees and grey cloaks. Time here seems to stand still.

argonath.name: The Argonath
argonath.text: Two stone kings stand over the river, their hands raised in warning.

amon-hen.name: Amon Hen
amon-hen.text: The fellowship breaks. Frodo and Sam go on alone.

emyn-muil.name: Emyn Muil
emyn-muil.text: A maze of sharp rock, and someone following at night.

dead-marshes.name: The Dead Marshes
dead-marshes.text: Pale lights in the water. Don't follow them.

morannon.name: The Black Gate
morannon.text: Too well guarded. There must be another way in.

ithilien.name: Ithilien
ithilien.text: Herbs, pines and fresh air: a garden land on the edge of darkness.

henneth-annun.name: Henneth Annûn
henneth-annun.text: A cave behind a waterfall and a hard choice for a captain.

crossroads.name: The Cross-roads
crossroads.text: A broken statue of a king, crowned again with little white flowers.

minas-morgul.name: Minas Morgul
minas-morgul.text: A pale, cold city across the valley. Don't look at it too long.

cirith-ungol-stairs.name: Stairs of Cirith Ungol
cirith-ungol-stairs.text: Endless steps up into the mountains. Your guide is smiling too much.

shelobs-lair.name: Shelob's Lair
shelobs-lair.text: A tunnel that smells wrong. A small light from a phial is all you have.

cirith-ungol-tower.name: Tower of Cirith Ungol
cirith-ungol-tower.text: Sam climbs the tower alone, singing in the dark.

isenmouthe.name: The Isenmouthe
isenmouthe.text: Roads full of soldiers. You crawl away in the confusion.

mount-doom.name: Mount Doom
mount-doom.text: The end of the road. The quest is done.

story.road-goes-on: The road starts at your own door, and it's hard to know where it will sweep you.
story.strider: The ranger leads you off the road, through bogs and midges.
story.rivendell-rest: Two months of rest in Rivendell are behind you. Nine companions: hobbits, a wizard, an elf, a dwarf and two men.
story.boats: Elven boats carry you down the great river for days.
story.gollum: A strange guide joins you. He talks to himself, and he knows the way.
story.burden: Every step is heavier than the last. Sam doesn't let go.

facts.bag-end-farm: Tolkien named Bag End after his aunt's farm in Worcestershire, which really was called Bag End.
facts.distance: This route is at real scale: by the Éowyn Challenge's reckoning, 1,779 miles (about 2,863 km) from Bag End to Mount Doom.
facts.one-novel: Tolkien wrote one long novel. The publisher split it into three volumes (1954–1955) to keep the price down.
facts.bombadil: Tom Bombadil began as a Dutch doll that belonged to Tolkien's son Michael.
facts.timeline: Frodo left Bag End on 23 September and reached Mount Doom on 25 March, about six months, with two months' rest in Rivendell and one in Lórien.
facts.languages: Tolkien said the stories grew out of his invented Elvish languages: the world was made so the languages would have somewhere to live.
facts.professor: Tolkien was an Oxford professor of Anglo-Saxon and knew many old languages, from Old Norse to Finnish.
facts.moria-name: In Sindarin, one of the Elvish languages, Moria means "black pit". The dwarves called their city Khazad-dûm. The walk through it is about 42 miles underground.
facts.inklings: Tolkien read chapters aloud to the Inklings, a circle of Oxford friends that included C. S. Lewis.
facts.boat-miles: Of the whole journey, 389 miles were travelled by boat, from Lórien down the Anduin to Rauros.
facts.somme: Tolkien fought in the Battle of the Somme in 1916. He later wrote that the Dead Marshes owe something to northern France after that battle.
facts.sam: Tolkien said Sam Gamgee was a reflection of the English soldiers and batmen he had known in the First World War.
facts.spider: Tolkien was born in Bloemfontein, South Africa, and was bitten by a tarantula as a toddler, though he said it gave him no special fear of spiders.
facts.maps: The maps in the first edition of The Lord of the Rings were drawn by Tolkien's son Christopher.
facts.film-volcano: In the films, Mount Doom was played by Ngauruhoe in New Zealand; you can walk past it on the Tongariro Crossing route.

dangers.rider-road: A Black Rider stops on the road and sniffs the air. You hide under the roots, and the Ring tugs at your hand.
dangers.rider-dusk: Hoofbeats again at dusk. A company of Elves comes singing through the trees, and the Rider slips away.
dangers.rider-hill: Looking back, you see a dark shape on the hill where you slept.
dangers.rider-cry: A long, cold cry from far off cuts your song short.
dangers.rider-ferry: As the ferry pulls away, a dark shape searches the landing on the far bank.
dangers.bree-night: At night the room you were meant to sleep in is torn apart.
dangers.weathertop-five: Five dark figures climb towards your fire. A cold blade finds Frodo's shoulder.
dangers.ford-nine: Nine Riders burst from the trees behind you as you race for the Ford.
dangers.wargs: Wolves howl around the camp at night, and the wizard's fire answers them.
dangers.shadow-flame: Drums in the deep, and a shadow of flame. The wizard holds the bridge.
dangers.winged-anduin: Somewhere over the river a winged shadow blots out the stars, until an elven arrow brings it down.
dangers.marsh-shadow: A winged shadow crosses the moon above the marshes, and every pale light goes out.
dangers.gate-shadow: A winged Rider circles over the Desolation. You lie flat in the dust.
dangers.morgul-host: The gates of Minas Morgul open and the Witch-king rides out at the head of an army.
dangers.in-the-dark: Something enormous moves in the tunnel ahead.
dangers.rider-overhead: Frodo feels a Rider pass high overhead, fleeing back towards the Dark Tower.
dangers.orc-march: An orc company takes you for deserters and drives you along the road.
